data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on Popper's terms as a methodological rule of 'rational faith' that explicitly rejects inductive justification, accepting the cost that this preference remains logically unjustifiable regarding future truth.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the agent believes the past success of the theory increases its objective probability of future success, the defense collapses into induction.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 'methodological rule' is claimed to be truth-conducive rather than merely expedient, it smuggles in induction.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Methodological Decisionism: Distinguishing between the logical status of a theory (which cannot be probabilified) and the pragmatic rationality of the scientist's choice to act on the theory that has withstood the most severe tests, treating this choice as a non-inductive convention.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
